Marico Limited has informed the Exchange regarding the report titled "Marico plans to raise Rs. 500 Crore" that was published on page 17 of The Economic Times, Mumbai, dated August 24,2006. Similar newspaper reports have appeared in some other newspapers, too. In this regard, the company has clarified as under:- Marico Limited (Marico) has not finalised any fresh financing plan, over and above the Long-Term Financing Plan that was approved by the Board on April 20,2006 and approved by shareholders on June 15,2006. The reports that appeared on August 24,2006 may create a wrong impression that the Company has finalised a fresh fund raising plan. Further, given below are the various facts in conenction with Marico's Financing Plan: 1) Marico's Board of Directors has on April 20,2006 approved a proposal regarding its Long-Term Financing Plan. The Company had, on the same day, informed the Stock Exchanges about this proposal. 2) This proposal was approved by the shareholders through a postal ballot, results of which were announced on June 15,2006 and filed with the Stock Exchanges on the same day. 3) The Company filed with the Stck Exchanges on August 18,2006 a Minuted copy of the resolutions passed by way of Postal Ballot, based on the results declared on June 15,2006. 4) Perhaps, the aforesaid minuted copy is being misinterpreted as a fresh resolution and thereby an impression may be gained that there is a fresh fund raising plan.

5) However, as would be obvious from the above, there is no further or fresh proposal of raising funds upto Rs. 500 crore or increasing the authorized capital of the company, beyond that already envisaged vide the Postal Ballot Resolution dated June 15,2006.

Marico Industries Ltd. has informed the Exchange that workers at the Goa Plant of the Company have declared a strike commencing on January 10, 2005, as the negotiations, arbitrated by the Labour commissioner, (that have been on for the past six months), have failed. The matter has been referred to the Industrial Tribunal for adjudication. Marico's Goa plant, engaged in manufacturing of coconut oil (CNO), is one of the three CNO plants that Marico operates in India, the other plants being at Pondicherry and Kanjikode. The short-term impact of this development is expected to be manageable, as the Goa plant has been contributing just about 14% of the total turnover and the Company has plans of servicing their markets through the Company's other plants, which have been hitherto operating at 65%-70% of their installed capacity.  The Company shall keep the Stock Exchange informed as the present situation gets resolved. A copy of this intimation has also been put up on the Company's website www.maricoindia.com for a wider dissemination of this information.

News Verification : The press had reports on July 21, 2004 that Marico Industries Limited is in the process of buying out the stake of Adil & Associates, in its joint venture company Kaya Skin Care Ltd.  The Exchange, in order to verify the accuracy or otherwise of the information reported in the press and to inform the market place so that the interest of the investors is safeguarded, had written to the officials of the company. The Company has vide its letter inter-alia stated that, "The company has announced Marico's purchase of the stake of its joint venture partner - Adil & Associates LLC (Adil) - in both, Kaya Skin Care Limited and Sundari LLC, for an undisclosed consideration subject to applicable statutory approvals. With this purchase, Kaya becomes a 100% subsidiary of Marico. Marico's stake in Sundari LLC goes up to 75.5%, the rest being held by Shantih LLC".
